nodes.summary: For a list $E$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers and natural numbers $u$ and $v$, the directed adjacency test of $E$ at $(u, v)$ is the boolean that is true exactly when the pair $(u, v)$ occurs in $E$, that is, when $E$ contains an edge from $u$ to $v$.
nodes.title: Directed adjacency in an edge list

nodes.summary: DIRECTED PATH COVER is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to an instance $(n, E, K)$ of DIRECTED PATH COVER that is well formed and feasible; bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.
nodes.title: DIRECTED PATH COVER as a decision problem

nodes.summary: An instance $(n, E, K)$ of DIRECTED PATH COVER is feasible when there is a list of at most $K$ paths, each a list of natural numbers, such that every path has no repeated vertex, every vertex on a path is less than $n$, and whenever $v$ immediately follows $u$ on a path the pair $(u, v)$ occurs in $E$; and such that every vertex $v < n$ lies on some path, and all paths containing $v$ are equal.
nodes.title: Feasible DIRECTED PATH COVER instances

nodes.summary: An instance of DIRECTED PATH COVER is a triple $(n, E, K)$, where the natural number $n$ is the number of vertices, the list $E$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers lists the directed edges, and the natural number $K$ bounds the number of paths.
nodes.title: Instances of DIRECTED PATH COVER

nodes.summary: The decision problem DIRECTED PATH COVER is in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to DIRECTED PATH COVER.
nodes.title: DIRECTED PATH COVER is NP-complete

nodes.summary: An instance $(n, E, K)$ of DIRECTED PATH COVER is well formed when the edge list $E$ has no repeated entries and every edge $(a, b)$ in $E$ satisfies $a < n$, $b < n$ and $a \ne b$.
nodes.title: Well-formed DIRECTED PATH COVER instances

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
